title: Rigel-Ladon: An Option-Count Law for a One-Pass Decision Encoder, Tested on Held-Out Option Counts and Held-Out Schemas
abstract: arXiv:2611.26332v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Laya is a small neural network that reads a text, a question and K written options, and returns one probability per option in a single pass. We ask how its accuracy falls as K grows from 2 to 35 and whether that can be predicted. We score nested option sets (every K-option question contains the smaller ones) on four question pools, for the released model (Base) and our fine-tune (FT), and score every item against each single rival. FT trained on one 12-option topic question (in-family); a 12-option HR (department-routing) question is out-of-family. Logit accuracy (the log of correct over incorrect answers) is linear in log(K-1) with slope 0.68 to 0.88. Fitted on K up to 6, the law predicts K=7 to 12 within 0.6 points and K up to 24 within 1.2 (a log-linear rule: 1.6 and 6.7). Taking the slope from the topic question and measuring only two-option accuracy on HR predicts its other K within 0.3 points (FT) and 0.7 (Base). On a 35-label pool

translated_title: Rigel-Ladon：一种针对单遍决策编码器的选项数定律——在留出选项数与留出题型上的测试
translated_abstract: Laya 是一个小型神经网络，它读取一段文本、一个问题和 K 个书面选项，并在单次前向传播中为每个选项输出一个概率。我们研究当 K 从 2 增长到 35 时其准确率如何下降，以及这种下降是否可以被预测。我们在四个问题池上对嵌套选项集（每个 K 选项问题都包含更小的选项集）进行评分，分别针对已发布的模型（Base）和我们的微调模型（FT），并将每个条目与每一个单一竞争对手进行评分。FT 在一个 12 选项的主题问题上训练（同类题型内）；而一个 12 选项的 HR（部门路由）问题属于异类题型。Logit 准确率（正确答案数与错误答案数之比的对数）在 log(K-1) 上呈线性关系，斜率为 0.68 至 0.88。基于 K≤6 的数据拟合，该定律预测 K=7 到 12 时误差在 0.6 分以内，K 到 24 时误差在 1.2 分以内（对数线性规则则分别为 1.6 和 6.7）。采用从主题问题取得的斜率，仅在 HR 任务上测量双选项准确率，即可预测其在其他 K 值下的准确率，误差在 0.3 分以内（FT）和 0.7 分以内（Base）。在一个 35 标签池上……
tldr: 该论文发现并验证了一条“选项数定律”：单遍决策编码器的 logit 准确率随 log(K-1) 线性下降（斜率 0.68–0.88），仅凭小选项数（K≤6）的测量即可精确预测留出的大选项数、甚至跨题型（如 HR 部门路由任务）的准确率。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes an "option-count law" for a one-pass decision encoder—logit accuracy falls linearly in log(K-1) with slope 0.68–0.88—enabling accurate prediction of held-out option counts and even held-out schemas from measurements at small K.
